Panel data: 50 firms × 5 years (2019-2023) = 250 observations. All 10 explanatory variables were z-score standardized (mean ≈ 0, SD ≈ 1). Dependent variable: Digital Transformation Comprehensive Technical Efficiency Value.

(1) F-test (Fixed Effects vs. Pooled OLS)
   - F statistic = 5.7865   (df1 = 50, df2 = 190)
   - p-value     = 0.000000e+00  (≈ 0)
   - Conclusion (α = 0.05): REJECT H0. The individual (firm) effects are jointly significant, so the Fixed Effects model is preferred over Pooled OLS.

(2) Hausman test (Fixed Effects vs. Random Effects)
   Note: Explanatory Variable 5 (Ownership Type) is time-invariant within firms and is absorbed by the fixed-effects estimator, so the Hausman test is performed on the 9 time-varying coefficients.
   - Chi-square statistic = 0.2796   (df = 9)
   - p-value              = 0.999998  (≈ 1)
   - Conclusion (α = 0.05): FAIL TO REJECT H0. No systematic difference between FE and RE coefficients, so the Random Effects model is consistent and efficient and is preferred over Fixed Effects.

Overall model-selection result: Pooled OLS rejected by F-test → FE/RE; Hausman non-significant → Random Effects model is the chosen specification for the standardized panel.
